name: Cursor
$comment: osTested is deliberately empty. Cursor 3.18.25 is installed on the machine this was written on and its shipped bundle was read directly, which is why the grades below are `source` rather than `docs` — but nobody has yet driven LeastGrant inside a running Cursor session. Reading the binary is strong evidence about the contract and no evidence at all about the integration. That distinction is the whole reason this file separates `source` from `probe`.

allow.note: Observed on beforeReadFile: an ordinary project file returned allow and the read completed.

deny.note: Observed, and stronger than expected: a deny on a command Cursor would otherwise auto-run without prompting was blocked outright. Cursor showed "Skipped", passed LeastGrant’s reason to the model verbatim — "you set a rule to always block this" — and the model reported it did not retry or work around the block. No afterShellExecution fired, because nothing ran.

ask.note: It reaches a person on beforeShellExecution — a curl-into-shell returned ask and Cursor raised its approval card with Skip / Always Run / Run, and the user approved it. It is `partial` because beforeReadFile has no ask at all: reads are allow-or-deny, so an unfamiliar read is allowed rather than questioned.

onCrash.note: Observed with failClosed: true as the installer writes it. A handler pointed at a script that does not exist blocked the call, and the model was told "Cursor blocked the terminal tool because a hook failed closed: ... returned no output."

onTimeout.note: Follows from failClosed on the gating events. Per-script timeout defaults to 60s.

timeoutDefaultSeconds.note: Per-script `timeout` in seconds; a warning is emitted above 3600.

canFailClosed.note: The installer sets failClosed: true on all three before* gates and it was observed doing what it says.

shell.note: beforeShellExecution fires before the command, and afterShellExecution after it. Round trip measured at 97–105 ms.

fileRead.note: Not a gate, and now measured rather than read. The beforeReadFile payload arrives with a `content` field already holding the file — all 86 bytes of the synthetic credential file, token included. Cursor had read it off disk before consulting the hook. A deny stops the content reaching the model, and the synthetic token appeared in no agent transcript; it does not prevent the read.

fileWrite.note: Measured: creating a file through Cursor’s edit tool produced ZERO hook invocations and no ledger entry. Not observed after the fact — invisible. Cursor registers no before-write, before-edit or before-delete step.

postToolUse.note: afterShellExecution and afterMCPExecution fire and are registered by the installer. LeastGrant answers them with no output, which Cursor logs as "produced no output" and treats as no opinion — correct for an after event, which cannot change anything.

exposesMode.note: No approval-mode field in any hook payload, although Cursor does have approvalMode internally (allowlist, unrestricted, auto-review).

modes.askSurvivesNote: On the two events that support it, an ask beats even the most permissive approval mode.

upstreamLimitations: File reads are observed after the fact, not gated. The beforeReadFile payload carries the file content, so the read has already happened by the time LeastGrant sees it. A deny stops the content reaching the model.
Writes, edits and deletes have no pre-execution event and are not intercepted at all. Measured: a file creation produced zero hook invocations.
beforeReadFile takes allow or deny and has no ask, so an unfamiliar read is allowed rather than questioned. Only a read LeastGrant recognises as a credential is blocked.
No permission mode reaches the hook, so LeastGrant cannot tell an attended session from an unattended one.
Cursor also ingests Claude Code hooks from .claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/settings.json, so installing both adapters may double-fire.

Cursor has its own sandbox and its own auto-run flow, and both act before the user sees anything. A command may be attempted sandboxed, blocked by that sandbox, and retried unsandboxed, with LeastGrant consulted separately each time.
There is no equivalent of Antigravity’s force_ask: nothing LeastGrant can return compels a prompt that the host’s own settings cannot satisfy.
leastgrantLimitations: MCP was not exercised in the live run — beforeMCPExecution is registered and was never invoked, so its behaviour is contract-derived.
Verified on Windows only. The POSIX transport passes the payload on native stdin rather than through PowerShell and has not been exercised.
The hook timeout was not tested; only the crash path was.

live.what: Human-assisted run through the real Cursor 3.18.25 IDE on a disposable workspace with a synthetic .env, with a transparent wrapper capturing the wire bytes and Cursor’s own hooks log read alongside. Six cases, all passed. Established: Cursor loads ~/.cursor/hooks.json and registers all five steps (from its own log, "Loaded 5 user hook(s)"); an ask raises the approval UI on beforeShellExecution; a deny blocks a command Cursor would otherwise auto-run, reaching the model verbatim; a credential read is denied and the value reaches no transcript, while the payload proves the file was already read; a file write fires no hook at all; and failClosed blocks when the handler cannot run.

transport.what: Observed rather than reproduced. Cursor delivers the payload through PowerShell with a UTF-8 BOM — first bytes ef bb bf on every one of the fourteen captured invocations — which is the bug that once had LeastGrant refusing every Cursor tool call. Parsed correctly throughout, 87–105 ms round trip. The payload carries conversation_id, generation_id, model, command or file_path, cwd, sandbox, session_id, cursor_version, workspace_roots, user_email and transcript_path; beforeReadFile adds content and attachments; afterShellExecution adds output and duration.

contract.what: The 21-step event list, response validator, failClosed handling and the post-execution nature of beforeReadFile read from the shipped 42 MB workbench and extension-host bundles.

mechanism: Per-step command hooks in ~/.cursor/hooks.json, on the three before* gates plus two after* events for learning. On Windows the payload is delivered through PowerShell from a temp file rather than on stdin.

controlPaths.what: rules files a later session follows
